title: Hiring young Bud Powell for a Village Corners gig
summary: Butler heard a baby-faced pianist playing, asked his mother's permission on Convent Place, took Bud Powell on a gig, and decided around 1946-47 to return to Europe.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I heard some fellow down there, and I heard so much of that man, and everything, said -- and he was a lad. He was just a baby, didn't shave, great big eyes, big-baby eyes, pretty eyes. He was taking care of that piano.
And there was another one called Timmy, the same thing.

with Art Hodes And so, about doing Dixieland work/and all, well, sometimes the people asked me to form a band, so, I had a job, I think it was a place called the Village Corners, and I heard this boy and I said, he was a -- so, I said, he said, you will have to ask my mother. She lived on Convent Place.
And I went to see his mother and she says yes, I can feed my son to you. It seemed so that she had confidence in me and Bud was a bit frantic then. Young boy.
You know, just happy and -- nervous and everything and I took him on the gig and people stood around, and that was, he was the belle of the ball.

He was wailing and didn't realize what he was doing, and so I took him home and paid him his money and then later, well, I didn't see him often because I was playing Dixieland, he was being young, you know and that is Bud Powell at that time.
About what year was this, do you remember what year?
Well, this would have been around 1946, or '47, yeah, '46 or '47 and I was going back to Europe.
I had decided definitely that I was going back Now, I sailed --
